newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Dominguez corrects after strong start.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Dominguez corrects after strong start.

text.p: Spanish fashion house Adolfo Dominguez, in its first day of public trading, was losing ground after a strong beginning as dealers started to take profits.
At 1105 GMT, the shares were trading at about 5,950, off 15 percent from its opening at 7,000 pesetas.
But the price remained strongly higher than the initial public offer for institutional investors at 3,100. The IPO retail price was at 3,007 pesetas per share.
Spain regulations limit a single share from losing or gaining more than 15 percent in a single trading day.
Dealers said the share price rise was amazing and added that profit taking should be considered normal at this level.
"This is incredible...with other IPOs we already had brisk rises but not so sharp. Even the lead managers were surprised," a trader in Madrid said.
"At this point it's normal to see a profit-taking wave, That should continue in the coming days," he added.
